main_issue: No representative cases or evidence refs are attached to this boundary. The ledger row itself acknowledges that the old guideline over-focused on URI schemes while the evidence supports a broader final-destination policy boundary. Without at least one source-reviewed case showing unsafe scheme handling as the primary bypass mechanism (with a concrete source-to-sink trace, exploit precondition, and fix evidence), semantic coherence cannot be assessed.

The mechanism is coherent across both representative cases: attacker-controlled destination (login redirect state / HTTP request parameter) reaches a browser-visible navigation sink (window.location.href / response.sendRedirect) without a final normalized destination policy check. The safe-fix semantics (parse, normalize, resolve against origin, reject unsafe schemes) apply consistently to both server-side and client-side sinks. The chamilo case provides fix-side validation but is not used as primary evidence, which is appropriate.
